content:
Although this week's iOS 27 public beta has stolen the spotlight, Apple has also released a new public beta firmware for AirPods at the same time. This update finally brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods public beta details

The AirPods public beta firmware version is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models can be updated:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 (Active Noise Cancellation version)
  • AirPods Max 2

You can enrol in the AirPods public beta through the Settings app on your iPhone. Once your AirPods are connected, a toggle option will appear in the Settings app, allowing you to enable the beta firmware. After that, as long as your AirPods are in their charging case and within range of your paired iPhone, the beta will automatically download and install.

  • Open the Settings app
  • Tap on "Bluetooth"
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and enable "AirPods Beta Updates"

Custom EQ officially arrives on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, you'll discover a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.

With the new custom EQ controls, you can fine-tune the sound profile of your AirPods. In the Settings app, you can adjust the bass, mid, and treble of your AirPods.

Apple explains: "AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully reproduce the original sound of music, TV shows, movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customise how your AirPods sound when playing any audio."

While adjusting the custom EQ, you can play songs from Apple Music directly in the Settings app to hear the adjustments in real time.

This is by no means the most advanced equaliser feature currently available—just a basic three-band system. But regardless, this is something AirPods users have waited a long time for, and Apple has finally given users the freedom to customise—although most people will probably stick with the default settings.

You can find the new custom EQ feature under the "Audio & Routing" menu in the AirPods section of the Settings app. All AirPods equipped with the H2 chip support this feature, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods

Below are other new features that iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned Settings app: iOS 27 has redesigned the AirPods interface in the Settings app. The control options have been reorganised, with hearing health, Find My, Live Translation, and other features separated into independent menus.
  • Adaptive Audio slider: A new slider has been added to the Settings app, allowing you to fine-tune the Adaptive Audio mode.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for years, it has always required pairing with an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac mentioned, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding through the Find My app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a supported iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrapping up
